input.rationale: Section 3.4 grants us a convenience right, but on its face the notice is expressed as "one month" effective only at the end of a calendar month and, more materially, Section 3.4(b) conditions the right on uncapped "early termination charges" specified in Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, so the fallback cap of three months' fees is not met. We therefore target the fallback: operation 1 states our convenience notice in operative days (thirty (30) days' prior written notice of termination for convenience), and operation 2 caps any early termination charge at three (3) months' charges. IBM has no mid-term convenience exit - its only routes are material breach (3.3) and non-renewal at the end of a term on ninety (90) days' notice (3.2) - so the two Vendor-side fallback elements are already met. The preferred pro-rata refund of prepaid charges is noted but not pressed.

ops.newText: a. providing at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice of such termination for convenience to IBM; and

ops.oldText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
ops.newText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, capped at three (3) months' charges.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have stated our convenience termination notice expressly as thirty (30) days' written notice and capped any early termination charge at three (3) months' charges, consistent with our fallback position that leaving on notice should not carry an open-ended penalty.
proposal.summary: State Customer's convenience notice in days and cap early termination charges at three months
